'''Samuel Aaron Adams''' (born June 13, 1973) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] for 14 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]], earning consensus [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors, and was selected eighth overall by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the [[1994 NFL draft]]. Following six seasons as a member of the Seahawks, he earned consecutive [[Pro Bowl]] selections and [[All-Pro]] honors during his two seasons with the [[Baltimore Ravens]]. Adams was also part of the team that won a [[Super Bowl]] title in [[Super Bowl XXXV]] and made another championship appearance in his one season for the [[History of the Oakland Raiders|Oakland Raiders]] in 2002. As a member of the [[Buffalo Bills]] from 2003 to 2004, Adams was named to a third Pro Bowl. He spent his last two seasons with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] and the [[Denver Broncos]].

'''Samuel Lewis Cunningham Jr''' (August 15, 1950 – September 7, 2021), nicknamed "'''Bam'''",<ref>Chapin, Dwight - McKay's Message Puts the Bam Back in Sam. Los Angeles Times, October 15, 1971.  "The name-Sam (Bam) Cunningham--makes you think of a big guy crunching through tacklers like a truck going through a plate glass window."</ref> was an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Fullback (gridiron football)|fullback]] who played in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for 10 seasons with the [[New England Patriots]].<ref>[https://usctrojans.com/news/2021/9/7/usc-trojans-football-sam-bam-cunningham-passes-away-nfl-new-england-patriots-rose-bowl.aspx Ex-USC, New England Patriots Star Fullback Sam "Bam" Cunningham Dies At 71]</ref> He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]], where he earned first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors and was the MVP of the [[1973 Rose Bowl]].

Selected in the first round of the [[1973 NFL draft]] by the Patriots, Cunningham became the franchise's all-time leading rusher. He was inducted to the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 2010. The same year, he was also inducted to the [[New England Patriots#Patriots Hall of Fame|Patriots Hall of Fame]].

'''Saleem Abdul'''<ref name="sex">{{cite news|last1=Faulk|first1=Kent|title=Former University of Alabama and NFL linebacker Saleem Rasheed begins serving time on plea to teacher sex charges|url=http://blog.al.com/spotnews/2013/08/former_university_of_alabama_a_1.html|access-date=December 26, 2016|work=AL.com|date=August 12, 2013}}</ref> '''Rasheed''' (born June 15, 1981) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

Rasheed played [[high school football]] at [[Shades Valley High School]] in [[Birmingham, Alabama]]. As a senior, he was named the state's [[Gatorade Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Saleem Rasheed 1998 - 1999 ALABAMA FOOTBALL PLAYER OF THE YEAR |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/saleem-rasheed/22211 |publisher=[[Gatorade]] |access-date=28 July 2021}}</ref>

Rasheed played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|University of Alabama]] between 1999 and 2001. He was selected to the [[2001 All-SEC football team]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Five Vols Named to Associated Press All-SEC Teams |url=https://utsports.com/news/2001/12/4/Five_Vols_Named_to_Associated_Press_All_SEC_Teams.aspx |access-date=28 July 2021 |publisher=[[Tennessee Volunteers|University of Tennessee Athletics]] |date=December 4, 2001 |language=en}}</ref>

Rasheed was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the third round of the [[2002 NFL draft]] with the 69th overall pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2002 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2002/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-18 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> As a rookie in 2002, he missed substantial playing time due to a nagging [[quadriceps]] injury.<ref name="2002injuries">{{cite news |last1=Lynch |first1=Kevin |title=49ERS' NOTEBOOK / Injured Rasheed out for Saturday's game |url=https://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/49ERS-NOTEBOOK-Injured-Rasheed-out-for-2710251.php |access-date=28 July 2021 |work=[[SFGATE]] |date=20 December 2002}}</ref> He also played for the [[Houston Texans]] though he was cut during the 2006 preseason.

The [[Calgary Stampeders]] signed him on May 7, 2008.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://cfldigest.com/stamps-sign-ex-nfler-rasheed/|title=Stamps sign ex-NFLer Rasheed|date=May 7, 2008|publisher=CFL Digest|access-date=May 4, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090606092715/http://cfldigest.com/stamps-sign-ex-nfler-rasheed/|archive-date=June 6, 2009|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>  He helped the Stampeders win the [[96th Grey Cup|2008]] [[Grey Cup]]. On May 4, 2009, he was released.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.tsn.ca/cfl/story/?id=277508|title=Stampeders release Sankey, three others|date=May 4, 2009|publisher=TSN.ca|accessdate=May 4, 2009}}</ref>

From 2009 to 2011 he worked as a teacher and coach at [[E.B. Erwin High School|Erwin High School]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://crime.blogs.tuscaloosanews.com/11348/ex-ua-nfl-linebacker-charged-with-welfare-fraud/|title=Ex-Alabama, NFL linebacker charged with welfare fraud|publisher=tuscaloosanews.com|accessdate=February 9, 2012|archive-date=February 4, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120204191625/http://crime.blogs.tuscaloosanews.com/11348/ex-ua-nfl-linebacker-charged-with-welfare-fraud/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In February 2012, Rasheed was charged with [[Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program|food stamp]] [[fraud]] and falsifying documents in [[Birmingham, Alabama]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.waff.com/story/16663998/former-nfl-linebacker-charged-in-ala-with-fraud|title=Former NFL linebacker charged in Ala. with fraud|date=February 2, 2012|publisher=waff.com|accessdate=February 2, 2012}}{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> He pleaded guilty to receiving $5,551 in food stamps while falsely claiming to be unemployed and, in July 2012, he was sentenced to eight months in prison. Rasheed also pleaded guilty to immigration fraud arising from his allegedly marrying a Moroccan woman and subsequently marrying an American woman without divorcing his first wife. In April 2013, Rasheed was sentenced to three years in prison for having sex with two students while a teacher at [[Woodlawn High School (Birmingham, Alabama)|Woodlawn High School]] in Birmingham. Although the students were at or above the [[Ages of consent in the United States#Alabama|age of consent in Alabama]], it is illegal for a teacher to have sex with students in the state.<ref name="sex" />

'''Samuel Jacob Bradford''' (born November 8, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[quarterback]] for nine seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL).

Bradford attended [[Putnam City North High School]], where he starred in football, basketball and golf. As a senior quarterback in 2005, he threw for 2,029 yards and 17 [[touchdown]]s in 12 games. Bradford was not highly recruited coming out of high school, but he received a scholarship offer from the [[University of Oklahoma]], which he accepted. After a [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirt season]] in 2006, Bradford threw for 3,121 yards and 36 touchdowns as a redshirt freshman with the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]]. In 2008, Bradford became only the second sophomore to win the [[Heisman Trophy]] as he led the highest-scoring offense in NCAA history, passing for 4,720 yards with 50 touchdowns and just eight [[interception]]s. He again led the nation in passing and also added five rushing touchdowns as the Sooners went 12–1 and advanced to the [[2009 BCS National Championship Game|BCS national title game]].

Bradford declared for the NFL draft following the 2009 season and was selected by the [[St. Louis Rams]] with the [[List of first overall NFL draft picks|first overall]] selection in the [[2010 NFL draft]]. That year, Bradford set the record for most completions by a rookie in NFL history, which helped earn him the [[NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year Award|NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year]] award. Prior to the start of the 2015 season, the Rams traded Bradford along with a 2015 fifth-round pick to the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in exchange for quarterback [[Nick Foles]], a 2015 fourth-round pick, and a 2016 second-round pick. Following his 2015 campaign with the Eagles, in which he set career-highs in passing yards (3,725), completion percentage (65%) and yards per attempt (7.0), the [[Minnesota Vikings]] acquired Bradford after their starting quarterback [[Teddy Bridgewater]] was lost to a season-ending knee injury before the start of the season. Bradford signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] in 2018 and started three games, but was replaced by rookie [[Josh Rosen]] and eventually released.

'''Samuel Richard Darnold''' (born June 5, 1997)<ref name="Pro Football Ref">{{Cite web |title=Sam Darnold Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DarnSa00.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191111060025/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/D/DarnSa00.htm |archive-date=November 11, 2019 |access-date=March 2, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> is an American professional football [[quarterback]] for the [[Seattle Seahawks]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Darnold was selected third overall in the first round of the [[2018 NFL draft]] by the [[New York Jets]], where he spent his first three seasons. After injuries and inconsistent play, Darnold was traded to the [[Carolina Panthers]], alternating as a starter and backup for two seasons, and spent one season as a backup with the [[San Francisco 49ers]]. Darnold had a breakout year in 2024 with the [[Minnesota Vikings]] when he led them to the playoffs and earned [[Pro Bowl]] honors.
